record.what_it_does: WooCommerce is an open-source e-commerce plugin for WordPress that exposes store data (products, orders, customers, coupons, etc.) via a REST API layered on the WordPress REST API.
record.auth_notes: Each store owner generates a Consumer Key + Consumer Secret pair in wp-admin (WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API); this pair is used as HTTP Basic Auth credentials over HTTPS, or as OAuth 1.0a 'one-legged' signed parameters over plain HTTP. There is also a per-store 'Application Authentication Endpoint' (/wc-auth/v1/authorize) that lets a third-party app redirect a merchant to their own site to approve access and receive generated keys via callback — an OAuth-like flow, but it runs on each individual merchant's WooCommerce install, not a central vendor authorization server, so it is not true multi-tenant OAuth2.
record.access_notes: WooCommerce is a free WordPress plugin; any developer can install it (or use a free sandbox/dev site) and generate REST API keys immediately from their own wp-admin with no approval or payment required. The catch is that API access is inherently per-store/self-hosted — there is no central vendor account to sign up for.
record.main_blocker: no central OAuth2/authorization server — each merchant's self-hosted store issues its own API keys, so onboarding is per-tenant

evidence.quote: You may use HTTP Basic Auth by providing the REST API Consumer Key as the username and the REST API Consumer Secret as the password.
This endpoint can be used by any APP to allow users to generate API keys for your APP.
New keys can be generated either through the WordPress admin interface or they can be auto-generated through an endpoint.
WooCommerce includes native support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling AI assistants and tools to interact directly with WooCommerce stores
The current and recommended version of the WooCommerce REST API. Use `/wp-json/wc/v3/` endpoints for all new integrations.

record.open_questions: Whether the official MCP integration (developer preview, feature-flagged) is stable enough for production toolkit use, and how it authenticates when using the shared WordPress MCP adapter vs. the deprecated WooCommerce-specific endpoint.
